chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, from Suleiman ibn Abbad, from Isa ibn Abu al-Ward, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Children of Israel complained to Musa (peace be upon him) about the whiteness (vitiligo) they were suffering from, so he took that complaint to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: 'Order them to eat the meat of the cow with the beet (or leek/green vegetable).'

key_terms.السِّلْقِ: Beet or leek (a type of green vegetable)

ai.seo_question: What was the remedy prescribed by Allah for the Children of Israel's skin disease according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the specific medical remedy prescribed during the Israelites' trial with the cow, linking the consumption of cow meat with *al-silq* (often interpreted as leeks or garlic) to alleviate 'al-bayad' (whiteness or vitiligo). Shia scholars utilize this text to highlight the intersection of divine revelation and practical health remedies, emphasizing that the command was not merely ritualistic but addressed a tangible physical affliction. It serves as a foundational reference in Islamic jurisprudence for understanding the medicinal aspects of dietary laws derived from Quranic narratives.
